[0780A]VERS. 4.-- *Ad nihilum deductus est,* etc. Ista perfectio est, ut nihil in homine valeat malignus. Et ut nihil sit in *conspectu ejus,* certissime noverit malignum non esse, nisi cum animus a suo Creatore aeterno et incommutabili ad creaturae speciem avertitur, quae de nihilo facta est. *Timentes autem Dominum glorificat,* qui potest dicere cum Propheta: *Mihi autem nimis honorificati sunt amici tui, Deus.*

*Qui jurat proximo suo et non decipit,* etc. Ista non sunt magna: sed qui nec ista potest, multo minus potest *loqui veritatem in corde suo,* et non agere *dolum in lingua sua,* sed ut est in corde, verum ita proferre, et habere in ore Est, est, Non, non, *et non facere proximo suo malum,* id est nulli homini; et [0780B] *opprobrium non accipere adversus proximum suum,* quae sunt perfectorum, in conspectu quorum ad nihilum deductus est malignus. Tamen etiam ista minora ita concludit

VERS. 5.-- *Qui facit haec, non movebitur in aeternum.*

## IN PSALMUM XV.

Rex noster in hoc psalmo loquitur ex persona susceptionis humanae, de quo titulus regalis tempore passionis inscriptus emicuit: *Jesus Nazarenus rex Judaeorum.* Sed ipsi in hoc loco veraciter Judaei intelliguntur, qui fidem Christi corde retinent ad justitiam, et ore confitentur in salutem.

VERS. 1, 2.-- *Conserva me, Domine, quoniam speravi in te. Dixi Domino: Deus meus es tu, quoniam [0780C] bonorum meorum non eges.* Quoniam *bonis meis* non exspectas tu fieri beatus. Quae verba, si ex persona Domini accipienda sunt, notandum valde quam aptissime congruant titulo, qui in Hebraico ita legitur: *humilis et simplicis Dei,* illius videlicet qui dixit: *Discite a me, quia mitis sum, et humilis corde.* Animadvertendum quoque, quod solus ille veraciter *Dominus* sit, qui, secundum quod hic excellentissime definitur, bono servi non eget. Non enim Deo, sed nobis praestamus, si bene agimus.

VERS. 3.-- *Sanctis qui sunt in terra ejus,* etc. Sanctis qui in terra viventium spem suam posuerunt, civibus Hierusalem coelestis, quorum conversatio spiritualis per anchoram spei in illa patria figitur, [0780D] quae recte *Dei terra* nominatur, quamvis adhuc in his terris carne versentur, *miras fecit* Pater *voluntates meas* in profectu illorum, quo senserunt quid eis profuerit et humanitas meae divinitatis ut morerer, et divinitas humanitatis ut resurgerem.

VERS. 4.-- *Multiplicatae sunt infirmitates eorum,* etc. Hae *infirmitates* errores sunt, quas per Evangelicam doctrinam multas in se esse cernentes *acceleverunt* salutem expetere a Christo.

*Non congregabo conventicula eorum de sanguinibus,* etc. Erunt ergo conventicula eorum non carnalia, nec *de sanguinibus* pecorum propitiatus congregabo eos, sed spirituali mutatione obliviscentur [0781A] quid fuerint; nec a me jam et peccatores, et amici, et homines, sed justi et fratres mei, et filii Dei vocabuntur.

VERS. 5.-- *Dominus pars haereditatis meae et calicis mei,* etc. Possidebunt enim mecum *haereditatem* ipsum Dominum. Eligant sibi alii partes, quibus fruantur, terrenas et temporales: portio sanctorum Dominus aeternus est. Bibant alii mortiferas voluptates: portio *calicis mei* Dominus est. Quod dico, *mei,* adjungo Ecclesiam, quia ubi caput ibi et corpus. Nam in haereditate *congregabo conventicula eorum,* et per calicis ebrietatem obliviscar nomina vetera eorum, ut nota sit et his, quos libero, claritas, qua eram apud te, o Pater, priusquam mundus fieret. Non enim *restitues* mihi quod non amisi, sed *restitues* his, qui [0781B] amiserunt, ejus claritatis notitiam, in quibus, quia ego sum, restitues.

VERS. 6.-- *Funes ceciderunt mihi in praeclaris,* etc. Limites passionis meae in tua claritate tanquam sorte *ceciderunt,* velut possessio sacerdotum et Levitarum Deus est. Quae autem sit ejus praeclara haereditas, manifestius in Hebraico, conversione ad Dominum facta, sic exponit: *Et tu haereditas speciosa mea es.*

VERS. 7.-- *Benedicam Dominum qui tribuit mihi intellectum,* etc. Eo quippe *intellectu* ista haereditas videri et possideri potest. Super intellectum autem usque ad mortem me erudivit inferior pars, mea carnis assumptio, ut experirer tenebras mortalitatis, quas ille intellectus non habet.

[0781C]VERS. 8.-- *Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper,* etc. Veniens enim in ea quae transeunt, non abstuli oculum ab eo qui semper manet, hoc *providens,* ut in eum per temporalia peracta recurrerem, qui mihi semper *a dextris est,* ut stabiliter in eo permaneam.

VERS. 9.-- *Propter hoc laetatum est cor meum,* etc. Ac si aperte dicat: Propter hoc et in cogitationibus meis jucunditas, et in verbis exsultatio. *Insuper et caro* non deficiet in interitum, sed in spe resurrectionis obdormiet.

VERS. 10.-- *Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno,* etc. Nam neque animam meam inferis possidendam dabis, neque sanctificatum corpus, per quod et alii sanctificandi sunt, corrumpi [0781D] patieris.

*Notas mihi fecisti vias vitae,* etc. *Notas fecisti* per me humilitatis *vias,* ut ad *vitam* redirent homines, unde per superbiam ceciderunt. In qua *adimplebis* eos *laetitia,* ut non ultra quaerant aliquid, cum facie ad faciem viderint te, in quibus, quia ego sum, *me adimplebis. Delectatio* est in favore et propitiatione tua, in hujus vitae itinere perducens usque ad finem gloriae conspectus tui.



## IN PSALMUM XVI.

Hoc est personae Domini tribuendum, adjuncta Ecclesia, quae corpus, ejus est.

VERS. 1.-- *Exaudi, Domine, justitiam meam,* etc. [0782A] Apud Dominum certum est habere *justitiam* vocem suam, quae res tacitas intelligentiae suae virtute cognoscit. Ipsius enim est oratio perfecta, cujus et causa clamat et lingua. *Non in labiis dolosis,* hoc est, non ad te *in labiis dolosis* procedentem. Bene enim orat, in cujus labiis dolus non est.

VERS. 2.-- *De vultu tuo judicium meum prodeat,* etc. Ex illuminatione notitiae tuae verum judicem. Aut certe *de vultu tuo* ait secundum illa quae in me respicis atque cognoscis. Hoc autem ille recte petebat, qui se noverat pollutionem non habere peccati.

VERS. 3.-- *Probasti cor meum et visitasti nocte,* etc. Probatum est cor meum visitatione tribulationis. Non autem *nox* tantum, quia perturbare assolet, [0782B] sed etiam *ignis,* quia urit, vocanda est ipsa tribulatio, qua examinatus justus inventus sum.

VERS. 4.-- *Ut non loquatur os meum opera hominum,* etc. Ut aliud non procedat ex ore meo, quam id quod pertineat ad gloriam tuam. Non ad *opera hominum,* qui faciunt praeter voluntatem tuam. *Propter verba* pacis tuae et prophetarum tuorum *ego custodivi vias laboriosas* mortalitatis humanae atque passionis.

VERS. 5.-- *Perfice gressus meos in semitis tuis,* etc. *Perficiatur* charitas Ecclesiae in itineribus angustis, quibus venitur ad requiem tuam. *Ut non moveantur signa itineris mei,* quae tanquam *vestigia* sacramentis et Scripturis apostolicis impressa sunt, quae intueantur et observent, qui me sequi volunt. [0782C] Aut certe ut jam stabiliter in aeternitate permaneam, posteaquam peregi vias duras, et in angustis semitarum tuarum gressus perfeci.

VERS. 6.-- *Ego clamavi, quoniam exaudisti me,* etc. Qui clamat, quoniam exauditur, utique purus, innocens, et immaculatus agnoscitur: nam confidenter oravit, quoniam se audiri posse de conscientiae puritate praesumpsit. Aut certe ita intelligendum: Ego liberam et validam intentionem precis ad te direxi, quoniam ut hanc habere possem, exaudisti me infirmius orantem. Non ergo deserat exauditio tua humilitatem meam.

VERS. 7.-- *Mirifica misericordias tuas, qui salvos facis sperantes in te,* etc. Non vilescant misericordiae tuae, ne minus amentur.

[0782D]VERS. 8.-- *A resistentibus dexterae tuae,* etc. *A resistentibus* favori, quo mihi faves, *custodi me ut pupillam oculi,* quae apparet parva et exigua, per eam tamen dirigitur acies luminis, quo lux et tenebrae dijudicantur: sic per Christi humanitatem divinitas judicii, discernens inter justos et peccatores.

*Sub umbra alarum tuarum protege me,* etc. Id est, sub munimento charitatis et misericordiae tuae protege me.

VERS. 9.-- *Inimici mei animam meam circumdederunt,* etc. *Inimici* ejus Judaei, *animam* ipsius, id est, vitam temporalem, *circumdantes* eum eripere quaesierunt.

[0783A]VERS. 10.-- *Qui adipem suum concluserunt.* Id est, laetitia sua pingui cooperti sunt, posteaquam cupiditas eorum de scelere satiata est. Et propterea *os eorum locutum est superbiam: Non habemus regem nisi Caesarem;* et, *qui destruis templum,* et caetera talia.

VERS. 11.-- *Projicientes me nunc circumdederunt me,* etc. *Projicientes* me extra civitatem, nunc *circumdederunt me* in cruce, et intentionem cordis sui *statuerunt declinare* in ista terrena, putantes magnum malum perpeti eum qui occidebatur.

VERS. 12.-- *Susceperunt me sicut leo paratus ad praedam,* etc. *Susceperunt* me, sicut ille adversarius circuiens quaerens quem devoret, *et sicut catulus ejus,* populus scilicet, cui dictum est: *Vos ex patre [0783B] diabolo estis,* cogitans de insidiis, quibus justum circumveniret et perderet.

VERS. 13.-- *Exsurge, Domine, praeveni eum et supplanta eum,* etc. *Exsurge,* Deus, quem dormire infidelis populus arbitratur, et iniquitates hominum non curare, antequam exerceatur malitia sua, ut factum ejus vindicta praeveniat, et ita *supplanta eum. Erue* autem *animam meam,* resuscitando me a morte, quae mihi ab impiis irrogata est. Anima autem mea *framea* tua est, quam assumpsit manus tua, id est aeterna virtus tua, ut per ipsam regna debellet iniquitatis, et dividat justos ab impiis. Hanc ergo erue ab inimicis meis.

VERS. 14.-- *Domine, a paucis de terra divide eos,* etc. *Pauci* sunt boni ad comparationem malorum; [0783C] sed *divisi* Judaei per orbem sunt *a paucis,* qui ex eis crediderunt, de Ecclesia, quae *terra* viventium, separati *in vita* ipsorum, id est, in ista, quam solam suam vitam putant, quia aeternam desperant. Non solum autem ista poena eos consecuta est visibilis, sed etiam de peccatis, quae tanquam tenebrae *absconduntur* a lumine veritatis Dei, *adimpleta* est memoria eorum, ut obliviscerentur Deum.

*Saturati sunt filiis, et dimiserunt reliquias suas parvulis suis;* hoc est, malorum operum fructibus sunt repleti, et peccata infidelitatis suae etiam suis posteris reliquerunt.

VERS. 15.-- *Ego autem in justitia tua apparebo,* etc. Ego autem qui non apparui eis qui corde sordido et tenebroso lucem sapientiae videre non possunt, [0783D] *in jnstitia tua* videbo faciem tuam, et *satiabor, cum apparuerit gloria tua,* ut hi qui me intelligunt. Diligenter vero notandum, et solerter est memoriae inculcandum, quam perspicue gloria resurrectionis fidelium juxta editionem Hebraicam his novissimis versiculis declaretur, quibus dicitur: *Ego in justitia videbo faciem tuam; implebor, cum evigilavero, similitudine tua.* Nam cum constet quod, nisi justificatum corpus Christi gratia ejus faciem Dei, qui justitiae est fons, videre non possit, non solum de tam excellenti dono gratulatur, sed insuper impleri se similitudine ipsius, cum evigilaverit, id est resurrexerit, tota certitudine confidit. Quid enim est aliud, *implebor, cum evigilavero, similitudine tua,* [0784A] nisi quod beatus Joannes Apostolus ait: *Scimus quia, cum apparuerit, similes ei erimus: quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est.*



## IN PSALMUM XVII.

Quae est ista *dies,* in qua corpus Christi *de manu omnium inimicorum* suorum eripiendum se novit, nisi illa cujus gloriam in fine praecedentis psalmi evidenter expressit dicens: *Implebor, cum evigilavero, similitudine tua.* Cum enim Ecclesia Christi in evigilatione, id est resurrectione, impleta fuerit similitudine Dei, tunc non solum de manu caeterorum inimicorum ereptam se gratulabitur, sed et de manu Saul, per quem significatur mors, cui in resurrectione insultabunt sancti dicentes: *Ubi est, mors, victoria tua, [0784B] ubi est, mors, aculeus tuus?* Saul quippe, qui interpretatur *petitus,* mortis similitudinem gerit, de qua Scriptura dicit: *Deus mortem non fecit, nec laetatur in perditione viventium.* Et post pauca: *Impii autem manibus et verbis accersierunt illam.*

VERS. 2.-- *Diligam te, Domine, fortitudo mea, Dominus firmamentum meum,* etc. Loquitur haec Christus et Ecclesia, id est totus Christus, caput et corpus. *Diligam te, Domine,* per quem fortis sum, qui me firmasti, qui refugi ad te: refugi autem, quia liberasti me.

VERS. 3.-- *Deus meus adjutor meus, et sperabo in eum.* Qui mihi prius adjutorium vocationis tuae praestitisti, ut sperare in te possim. *Protector meus, et cornu salutis meae, et susceptor meus.* Protector [0784C] meus, quia non de me praesumpsi, quasi erigens adversum te cornu superbiae, sed teipsum cornu, hoc est, firmam celsitudinem salutis inveni: quod ut invenirem, suscepisti me.

VERS. 4.-- *Laudans invocabo Dominum,* etc. Non meam gloriam, sed Domini quaerens *invocabo Dominum,* et non erit unde mihi noceant impietatis errores.

VERS. 5.-- *Circumdederunt me dolores mortis,* etc. *Dolores* mortalitatis, hoc est carnis, *circumdederunt me,* et turbae iniquae ad tempus commotae velut flumina pluvialia cito desitura egerunt, ut conturbarent me.

VERS. 6.-- *Dolores inferni circumdederunt me,* etc. In his qui me circumdederunt, ut perderent, erant [0784D] *dolores* invidentiae, qui mortem operantur, perducuntque ad infernum peccati. Praevenerunt autem me, ut priores nocere vellent, quod eis postea redderetur. Tales autem homines capiunt in perditionem, quibus mala persuaserint jactatione justitiae, cujus non re sed nomine adversus gentes gloriantur.

VERS. 7.-- *In tribulatione mea invocavi Dominum,* etc. *De templo,* hoc est de corde meo, in quo habitat, *exaudivit vocem meam; et clamor meus,* quem non in auribus hominum, sed coram ipso intus habeo, *introivit in aures ejus.*

VERS. 8.-- *Commota est et contremuit terra, fundamenta montium conturbata sunt.* Clarificato Filio [0785A] hominis *commoti sunt et contremuerunt* peccatores, et spes superborum, quae in hoc saeculo fuerunt, conturbatae sunt, ut scilicet jam firmamentum non haberet in cordibus hominum spes temporalium bonorum.

VERS. 9.-- *Ascendit fumus in ira ejus,* etc. *Ascendit* lacrymosa deprecatio poenitentium, cum cognovissent quid minaret Deus impiis; et flagrantia charitatis de notitia ejus post poenitentiam *exarsit;* et illi, qui jam mortui erant, deserti ab igne boni desiderii ac luce justitiae, et frigidi tenebrosique remanserant, rursus *accensi* et illuminati revixerunt.

VERS. 10.-- *Inclinavit coelos et descendit,* etc. Apostolos humilitate informavit, et impii, qui terrena [0785B] sapiunt, *caliginem* malitiae suae non cognoverunt.

VERS. 11.-- *Et ascendit super cherubim et volavit,* etc. Exaltatus est super plenitudinem scientiae, ut nemo ad Dominum veniret nisi per charitatem. *Plenitudo enim legis est charitas;* et cito se incomprehensibilem esse monstravit dilectoribus suis, ne illum corporeis imaginationibus prehendere se posse arbitrarentur. Illa autem celeritas, qua se incomprehensibilem esse monstravit, super virtutes animarum est, quibus se velut pennis a terris in auras libertatis extollunt.

VERS. 12.-- *Et posuit tenebras latibulum suum. Posuit* obscuritatem sacramentorum, et occultam spem in corde credentium, ubi lateret ipse non eos [0785C] deserens. In his etiam *tenebris,* ubi per fidem adhuc ambulamus, non per speciem, quandiu quod non videmus speramus, et per patientiam exspectamus. Conversi tamen ad ipsum ambiunt eum, qui credunt ei, quia in medio eorum est, cum omnibus aequaliter favet, in quibus, tanquam in tabernaculo habitat hoc tempore. Nec propterea quisquam in illa luce, quae futura est, cum ex fide ad speciem venerimus, jam se esse arbitretur, si Scripturas recte intelligit: quia in prophetis, atque omnibus divini verbi praedicatoribus obscura doctrina est in comparatione fulgoris, qui est *in conspectu* manifestationis ejus. Unde et sequitur:

VERS. 13.-- *Prae fulgore in conspectu ejus nubes,* etc. *Nubes ejus,* id est praedicatores verbi ejus, [0785D] non jam in Judaeae finibus continentur, sed *transierunt* ad gentes. Objurgationes autem, quibus velut *grandine* corda dura tunduntur, si animus mitis et pius exceperit, in doctrinam satiantem resolvuntur; igne vero charitatis accenso corda reviviscunt. Haec omnia in nubibus ipsius ad gentes *transierunt.*

VERS. 14.-- *Et intonuit de coelo Dominus,* etc. Ut n profundo rerum humanarum audirentur coelestia.

VERS. 15.-- *Et misit sagittas suas, et dissipavit eos, fulgura,* etc. *Et misit* evangelistas pennis virtutum recta itinera transvolantes, non suis, sed ejus a quo missi sunt, ut aliis essent odor vitae in vitam, aliis odor mortis in mortem. *Multiplicavit* quoque miracula, *et conturbavit eos.*

[0786A]VERS. 16.-- *Et apparuerunt fontes aquarum,* etc. Revelati sunt prophetae, qui non intelligebantur, super quos aedificaretur orbis terrarum credens Domino. *Ab increpatione tua, Domine, ab inspiratione spiritus irae tuae;* clamantis scilicet: *Appropinquavit super vos regnum Dei;* et: *Nisi poenitentiam egeritis, omnes simul moriemini.*

VERS. 17.-- *Misit de summo et accepit me,* etc. Vocando ex gentibus in haereditatem gloriosam Ecclesiam non habentem maculam aut rugam, assumpsit me de multitudine populorum.

VERS. 18.-- *Eripuit me de inimicis meis fortissimis,* etc. *Eripuit me de inimicis meis,* qui praevaluerunt ad affligendam et pervertendam istam temporalem vitam meam.

[0786B]VERS. 19.-- *Praevenerunt me in die afflictionis meae,* etc. Priores mihi nocuerunt in tempore, quo mortale et laboriosum corpus gero; et quoniam amaritudine miseriarum firmamentum terrenae voluptatis contribulatum atque convulsum est, *factus est Dominus protector meus.*

VERS. 20.-- *Et eduxit me in latitudinem, salvum me fecit, quoniam voluit me.* Quia carnales patiebar angustias, *eduxit me* in spiritalem *latitudinem* fidei, *quoniam voluit me,* antequam ego illum vellem.

VERS. 21.-- *Et retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam,* etc. *Retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam* bonae voluntatis, qui prior praebuit misericordiam, antequam haberem bonam voluntatem; *et secundum puritatem factorum meorum,* qui [0786C] tribuit mihi, ut bene facerem, educendo me in latitudinem fidei.

VERS. 22.-- *Quia custodivi vias Domini, nec impie gessi a Deo meo.* Ut latitudinem bonorum operum, quae per fidem sunt, longanimitas perseverandi consequatur.

VERS. 23.-- *Quoniam omnia judicia ejus in conspectu meo,* etc. Id est, et praemia justorum, et poehas impiorum, et flagella corrigendorum, et tentationes probandorum perseveranti considero contemplatione. *Et justitias ejus non repuli a me,* quod faciunt deficientes sub sarcina earum, et revertentes ad vomitum suum.

VERS. 24, 25.-- *Et ero immaculatus cum eo, et observabo me ab iniquitate mea. Et retribuet mihi Dominus [0786D] secundum justitiam meam,* etc. Non solum propter latitudinem fidei, quae per dilectionem operatur, sed etiam propter longitudinem perseverantiae, *retribuit mihi Dominus,* non quod homines vident, *sed in conspectu oculorum ejus,* quoniam quae videntur, temporalia sunt; quae autem non videntur, aeterna sunt, quod pertinet ad altitudinem spei.

VERS. 26, 27.-- *Cum sancto sanctus eris, et cum viro innocente innocens eris; et cum electo electus eris, et cum perverso perverteris.* Est etiam occulta profunditas, qua intelligeris *cum sancto sanctus,* quia tu sanctificas, *et cum viro innocente innocens,* quia nulli noces, sed criniculis peccatorum suorum unusquisque constringit ur: et ab eo, quem eligis, [0787A] eligeris, et *cum perverso* videris *perversus,* quoniam dicunt: *Non est recta via Domini,* et ipsorum via non est recta.

VERS. 28.-- *Quoniam tu populum humilem salvum facies,* etc. Hoc perversum videtur perversis, quod confitentes peccata sua salvos facis, ignorantes autem Dei justitiam, et suam volentes constituere, *humilias.*

VERS. 29.-- *Quoniam tu illuminas lucernam meam,* etc. Non est nostrum lumen ex nobis, sed *tu illuminas lucernam meam, Domine:* nos enim peccatis nostris tenebrae sumus, sed Deus meus illuminabit tenebras meas.

VERS. 30.-- *Quoniam in te eripiar a tentatione, et in Deo meo transgrediar murum.* Non in me, sed *in [0787B] te eripiar a tentatione,* et non in me, sed *in Deo meo transgrediar murum,* quem inter homines et coelestem Hierusalem peccata erexerunt.

VERS. 31.-- *Deus meus impolluta via ejus, eloquia Domini igne examinata,* etc. *Deus meus* non venit in homines, nisi manducaverint viam fidei, qua veniat ad eos, quia *impolluta est via ejus. Eloquia* quoque *Domini igne* examinationis probantur, et omnes, qui non in se ipsis, sed in illo sperant, eadem tribulatione non consumuntur; spes enim sequitur fidem.

VERS. 32.-- *Quoniam quis Deus praeter Dominum aut quis Deus praeter Deum nostrum? Quis Deus praeter Dominum,* cui servimus? *et quis Deus praeter Deum nostrum,* quem post bonam servitutem tanquam haereditatem sperantes filii possidebimus?

[0787C]VERS. 33.-- *Deus, qui praecinxit me virtute, et posuit immaculatam viam meam. Praecinxit me,* ut fortis sim, ne defluentes sinus cupiditatis impediant opera et gressus meos. *Et posuit immaeulatam viam* charitatis, qua ad illum veniam, sicut impolluta est fides, qua venit ad me.

VERS. 34.-- *Qui perfecit pedes meos tanquam cervorum, et super excelsa statuens me. Qui perfecit* amorem meum ad transcendenda spinosa et umbrosa implicamenta hujus saeculi, et super coelestem habitationem figit intentionem meam, ut implear in omnem plenitudinem Dei.

VERS. 35.-- *Qui docet manus meas ad praelium,* etc. *Qui docet* me operari ad superandos inimicos, qui nobis intercludere coelestia regna conantur. [0787D] *Et posuisti* infatigabilem intentionem bonorum operum meorum.

VERS. 36.-- *Et dedisti mihi protectionem salutis tuae, et dextera tua suscepit me. Dedisti mihi protectionem salutis tuae,* et favor gratiae tuae suscepit me.

*Et disciplina tua correxit me in finem, et disciplina tua ipsa me doeebit.* Disciplina tua me deviare non sinens correxit, ut quidquid ago, in eum finem referam, quo haeretur tibi, et eadem disciplina tua me docebit pervenire, quo direxit.

VERS. 37.-- *Dilatasti gressus meos subtus me, et non sunt infirmata vestigia mea.* Nec impediunt carnales angustiae, quoniam latam fecisti charitatem meam operantem hilariter, etiam de ipsis quae subter [0788A] me sunt, mortalibus rebus et membris: *et non sunt infirmata* sive itinera mea, sive signa, quae impressi ad imitandum sequentibus.



## IN PSALMUM XVII. (cont.)

VERS. 38.-- *Persequar inimicos meos, et comprehendam illos, et non convertar donec deficiant. Persequar* affectus meos carnales, ne ab eis comprehendar, sed comprehendam illos, ut absumantur, et ab ista intentione *non convertar* ad quietem, *donec deficiant* qui obstrepunt mihi.

VERS. 39.-- *Confringam illos, nec poterunt stare, cadent subtus pedes meos. Confringam illos,* nec durabunt adversum me: directos illis proponam timores, quibus ambulo in aeternum.

VERS. 40.-- *Et praecinxisti me virtute ad bellum, supplantasti insurgentes in me subtus me.* Constrinxisti [0788B] fluentia desideria carnis meae virtute, ne in tali pugna praepedirer, et decipi fecisti eos qui me insequebantur, ut subter me fierent, qui super me esse cupiebant.

VERS. 41.-- *Et inimicos meos dedisti mihi dorsum,* etc. Inimicos meos convertisti, et dorsum mihi eos fecisti esse, id est ut sequerentur me, alios autem eorum, qui in odio perdurarunt, disperdidisti.

VERS. 42.-- *Clamaverunt, nec erat qui salvos faceret ad Dominum, nec exaudivit eos.* Quis enim salvos faceret, quos tu non faceres? Nec ad quemlibet, sed ad Dominum clamaverunt, nec exauditione dignos judicavit non recedentes a malitia sua, quod de Judaeis specialiter intelligendum est, qui in synagogis clamant, nec exaudiuntur, quia terrenam Hierusalem [0788C] desiderant, non coelestem.

VERS. 43.-- *Et comminuam eos ut pulverem ante faciem venti,* etc. Et aridi sunt non recipientes imbrem misericordiae Dei, ut elati superbia ab spe firma et inconcussa tanquam a terrae soliditate ac stabilitate rapiantur; *ut lutum platearum,* quia per latas, quas multi ambulant, perditionis vias luxuriantur et lubrici sunt.

VERS. 44.-- *Eripies me de contradictionibus populi,* etc. *Eripies me de contradictionibus* eorum qui dixerunt: *Si dimiserimus eum vivum, saeculum post illum abit.*

VERS. 45.-- *Populus quem non cognovi,* etc. *Populus* gentium, quem corporali praesentia non visitavi, servivit mihi: neque oculis me vidit, sed recipiens [0788D] praedicatores meos *in auditu auris obedivit mihi.*

VERS. 46.-- *Filii alieni mentiti sunt mihi,* etc. *Filii* non mei dicendi, sed potius *alieni,* quibus recte dicebatur: *Vos ex patre diabolo estis, mentiti sunt mihi: filii alieni,* quibus ut renovarentur, Novum Testamentum attuli, in vetere homine remanserunt, et tanquam uno pede debiles (quia Vetus tenentes Novum respuerunt) claudi effecti sunt, etiam in ipsa veteri lege potius suas traditiones sequentes quam Dei.

Calumniabantur enim de manibus non lotis, quia tales erant *semitae,* quas ipsi fecerant, et consuetudine triverant, aberrando ab itinere praeceptorum Dei.

[0789A]VERS. 47.-- *Vivit Dominus, et benedictus Deus meus,* etc. Non terrena consuetudine de Deo salutis meae sentio; nec terrenam ipsam salutem sed in excelso de illo sperem.

VERS. 48.-- *Deus, qui das vindictas mihi,* etc. Deus, qui vindicas me subdendo sub me populos, *liberator meus de inimicis meis.* Judaeis, clamantibus. Crucifige, crucifige!

VERS. 49.-- *Et ab insurgentibus in me exaltabis me,* etc. Ab eisdem insurgentibus in me patientem, exaltabis me resurgentem, atque a regno eorum iniquo eripies me.

VERS. 50.-- *Propterea confitebor tibi in nationibus, Domine,* etc. Propterea tibi pro me confitebuntur gentes, Domine, et latius innotesces bonis operibus [0789B] meis.

VERS. 51.-- *Magnificans salutes regis ejus,* etc. Deus magnificat, ut amabiles faciat salutes, quas ejus Filius dat credentibus, et *facit misericordiam Christo suo,* ipsi liberatori manu forti, qui vicit hunc mundum, et eis, quos credentes in Evangelio genuit in aeternum.

Quaecunque in hoc psalmo dicta sunt, quae ipsi proprie Domino, id est capiti Ecclesiae congruere non possunt, ad Ecclesiam referenda sunt. Totus enim hic Jesus loquitur, in quo sunt omnia membra ejus.



## IN PSALMUM XVIII.

Titulus notus est, nec Dominus Jesus Christus haec [0789C] dicit, sed de illo haec dicuntur.

VERS. 2.-- *Coeli enarrant gloriam Dei, et opera manuum ejus annuntiat firmamentum.* Justi evangelistae, in quibus Deus tanquam in coelis habitat, exponunt gloriam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, sive gloriam, qua glorificavit Patrem Filius super terram. Et facta virtutum Domini *annuntiat firmamentum:* fiducia quippe Spiritus sancti firmamentum et coelum factum est, quod antea timore terra erat.

VERS. 3.-- *Dies diei eructat verbum, et nox nocti indicat scientiam.* Spiritus spiritalibus profert plenitudinem incommutabilis sapientiae Dei, quod Verbum in principio Deus apud Deum est, et mortalitas carnis, tanquam longe positis carnalibus fidem insinuando annuntiat futuram scientiam.

[0789D]VERS. 4.-- *Non sunt loquelae neque sermones.* Per quas non auditae sunt voces evangelistarum, eum omnibus linguis Evangelium praedicaretur.

VERS. 5, 6.-- *In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terrae verba eorum. In sole posuit tabernaculum suum,* etc. Dominus, ut adversus regna temporalium errorum belligeraret, non pacem sed gladium missurus in terram, in tempore vel in manifestatione posuit tanquam militare habitaculum suum, hoc est, dispensationem incarnationis suae, procedens de utero virginali, ubi Dominus naturae humanae tanquam sponsus sponsae copulatus est. *Exsultavit ut gigas ac currendam viam suam,* etc. Exultavit ut fortissimus, et caeteros homines incomparabili [0790A] virtute praecedens, non ad habitandum, sed ad currendam viam. Et:

VERS. 7.-- *A summo coeli egressio ejus.* Id est, a Patre, non temporalis aequiparatio, sed aeterna, quae de Patre natus est. *Et occursus ejus usque ad summum ejus,* etc. Occurrit plenitudine divinitatis usque ad aequalitatem Patris. Cum autem Verbum etiam caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis, mortalitatem nostram suscipiens, non permisit ullum mortalium excusare se de umbra mortis, et ipsam penetravit verbi calor.

VERS. 8.-- *Lex Domini immaculata convertens animas,* etc. *Lex Domini,* id est, qui venit legem implere non solvere. Et *immaculata* lex, quia peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus, [0790B] non premens animas servitutis jugo, sed ad se imitandum libertate convertens. Cujus *testimonium fidele* est, quia nemo novit Patrem nisi Filius, et cui voluerit revelare, quae abscondita sunt a sapientibus, et revelata parvulis, quoniam Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam.

VERS. 9.-- *Justitiae Domini rectae, laetificantes corda,* etc. Omnes *justitiae Domini* in illo *rectae,* qui non docuit quod ipse non fecit, ut qui imitarentur, corde gauderent in eis, quia libere cum charitate facerent, non serviliter cum timore. Cujus praeceptum *lucidum* est, sine velamento scilicet carnalium observationum, *illuminans* hominis inferioris aspectum.

VERS. 10.-- *Timor Domini sanctus, permanens in [0790C] saeculum saeculi,* etc. *Timor Domini* non ille sub lege poenalis, temporalia bona sibi subtrahi perhorrescens, quorum dilectione anima inquinatur, sed *sanctus,* quo Ecclesia sponsum suum quanto ardentius diligit, tanto diligentius cavet offendere. Et ideo non foras mittit consummata dilectio timorem hunc, sed *permanet in saeculum saeculi. Judicia* quoque ejus, qui non judicat quemquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio, vere *justificata* incommutabiliter. Neque enim et minatus, et pollicitus Deus quemquem fallit, aut quisquam et impios supplicio ejus, et pios praemio ejus potest eripere.

VERS. 11.-- *Desiderabilia super aurum et lapidem pretiosum multum,* etc. Sive *multum* ipsum aurum et lapidem, sive *multum* pretiosum, sive *multum* [0790D] desiderabilia, tamen *desiderabilia judicia* Dei super pompas hujus saeculi, quarum desiderio fit, ut non desiderentur, sed timeantur, aut contemnantur, aut non credantur judicia Dei. Quod si quisque ipse sit aurum, lapisque pertiosus, ut igne non consumatur, sed assumatur in thesaurum Dei, plus quam seipsum desideret judicia ejus, cujus voluntatem praeponit suae; et sive quisque jam sit mel, quia solutus vitae hujus vinculis exspectat diem, quo veniat in epulas Dei; sive adhuc favus sit, ut quasi cera circumplicetur hac vita, non huic concretus, sed implens eam, cui opus sit aliqua pressura, non opprimentis, sed exprimentis manus Dei, qua de temporali vita in aeternum relinquetur: *dulciora* illi sunt [0791A] judicia Dei, quam sibi ipsi est, quia *super mel et favum* illa dulciora sunt.

VERS. 12.-- *Etenim servus tuus custodit ea,* etc. Ideo inquit, tam dulcia mihi sunt, quia custodio ea: nam non custodienti amara dies Domini. Itaque non in aliquo extra posito commodo, sed in eo ipso, quod judicia Dei custodiuntur, *multa retributio* est, quia gaudetur in eis.

VERS. 13.-- *Delicta quis intelligit? Ab occultis meis munda me,* etc. In *delictis* autem, qualis suavitas potest esse, ubi non est intellectus, quoniam *delicta quis intelligit?* Quae ipsum occultum claudunt, cui suavitas est veritas, cui desiderabiliora et dulciora sunt judicia Dei, et sicut tenebrae oculos, ita delicta mentem nec lucem sinunt videre, nec se. Ab [0791B] *occultis* ergo *meis,* inquit, *munda me,* Domine, nec seducas *ab alienis.* Neque enim ab alienis capitur, qui est mundus a suis. *Parce* itaque *ab alienis* cupiditatibus, non superbo, et in sua potestate esse cupienti, sed *servo tuo.*

VERS. 14.-- *Si mei non fuerint dominati,* etc. Hujus versiculi sensum manifestiorem facit ex Hebraeo translata editio, ubi legitur: *A superbis quoque libera servum tuum; si mei non fuerint dominati, tunc immaculatus ero:* superbi enim et alieni maligni spiritus intelliguntur ob immanitatem superbiae suae a Deo irremeabiliter alienati, quorum dominatio per peccatum humanum genus opressit. Cum ergo orasset superius dicens: *Ab occultis meis munda me,* congrue mox subdidit: *Si mei non fuerint [0791C] dominati, tunc immaculatus ero:* quia si superbi et alieni illi a Deo spiritus nullam in nobis peccati merito obtinuerint potestatem, tunc vere celeri remissione percepta immaculati erimus. Et quia radix ac fomes totius peccati superbia est, per quam et diabolus corruit, et primus homo mundo mortem induxit, etiam ab hoc *delicto maximo emundabimur* de potestate daemonum liberati, quorum princeps est dominator superborum, sicut de illo legitur: *ipse est rex super omnes filios superbiae.* Si autem legamus, ut in quibusdam codicibus habetur, *si mei non fuerint dominata, tunc immaculatus ero,* hic sensus est: si mei non fuerint dominata occulta mea et aliena, tunc immaculatus ero. Non enim est tertia origo peccati praeter *occultum* suum, quo cecidit [0791D] diabolus, et *alienum,* quo seductus est homo, ut consentiendo suum faceret. *Et emundabor,* inquit, *a delicto maximo,* superbiae scilicet: non enim est majus delictum, quam apostatare a Deo, quod est initium superbiae hominis. Et vere ille immaculatus est, qui etiam hoc delicto caret, quia hoc est ultimum redeuntibus ad Dominum, quod recedentibus primum fuit.

VERS. 15.-- *Et erunt ut complaceant eloquia oris mei.* etc. Meditatio cordis mei, non ad jactantiam placendi hominibus, quia jam nulla snperbia est, sed *in conspectu tuo semper,* qui conscientiam puram inspicis.

*Domine adjutor meus et Redemptor meus. Domine [0792A] adjutor meus* tendentis ad te, quoniam *Redemptor meus* es, ut tenderem ad te, ne quisquam et sapientiae suae tribuens, quod ad te convertitur, et viribus, quod ad te pervenit, magis repellatur abs te, qui superbis resistis, quia non est mundatus a delicto maximo, nec complacuit in conspectu tuo, qui redimis ut convertamur, et adjuvas, ut perveniamus ad te.



## IN PSALMUM XIX.

Notus est titulus, nec Christus dicit, sed Christo dicit Propheta, figura optandi, quae ventura sunt, canens:

VERS. 2.-- *Exaudiat te Dominus in die tribulationis, protegat te nomen Dei Jacob,* etc. *Exaudiat te* [0792B] Dominus *in die* qua dixisti: *Pater, salavifica me ex hac hora:* ad te enim pertinet populus, posterius natus, quia major serviet minori.

VERS. 3.-- *Mittat tibi auxilium de sancto,* etc. Faciens tibi sanctificatum corpus Ecclesiam, quae te tanquam de speculatione exspectat, quando venias a nuptiis.

VERS. 4.-- *Memor sit omnis sacrificii tui,* etc. Memores nos faciat omnium injuriarum tuarum, et contumeliarum, quas pro nobis pertulisti, et crucem, qua totus anima et corpore oblatus es Deo, in laetitiam resurrectionis convertat.

VERS. 5.-- *Tribuat tibi secundum cor tuum,* etc. *Tribuat tibi* non secundum cor eorum, qui putaverunt persequendo te posse deleri, sed *secundum cor [0792C] tuum,* qui scisti quid utilitatis haberet passio tua. *Et confirmet omne consilium tuum,* non solum quo animam posuisti pro amicis tuis, ut mortificatum granum copiosius surgeret, sed etiam, quo caecitas ex parte in Israel facta est, ut plenitudo gentium intraret, et sic omnis Israel salvus fieret.

VERS. 6.-- *Laetabimur in salutari tuo,* etc. *Laetabimur,* quod tibi mors nihil nocebit, ita enim eam nec nobis nocere posse monstrabis. Et confessio nominis tui non solum non perdet, sed etiam magnifibabit nos.

VERS. 7.-- *Impleat Dominus omnes petitiones tuas,* etc. *Impleat Dominus* non solum *petitiones* quas habuisti in terra, sed etiam quibus in coelo interpellas pro nobis. Nunc enim mihi per prophetiam [0792D] demonstratum est, quoniam resuscitabit Dominus Christum suum.

*Exaudiat illum de coelo sancto suo,* etc. *Exaudiat* illum non de terra tantum, ubi se petit clarificari, verum etiam *de coelo,* ubi jam ad dexteram Patris interpellans pro nobis diffudit inde Spiritum sanctum super credentes in se. *Potentatus* vero nostri sunt *salus* favoris ejus, cum etiam de tribulatione dat auxilium, ut quando infirmamur, tunc potentes simus. Nam vana salus hominum, quae non *dextera* sed sinistra ejus est: ecce enim extolluntur in magna superbia, quicunque peccantes temporaliter salvi facti sunt.

VERS. 8.-- *Hi in curribus et hi in equis, nos autem [0793A] in nomine Domini Dei nostri invocabimus.* Hi volubili successione temporalium bonorum trahuntur, et hi superbi efferuntur, honoribus, atque in his exsultant. Nos autem spem figentes in aeternis, neque gloriam nostram quaerentes, *In nomine Domini Dei nostri exsultabimus.*

VERS. 9.-- *Ipsi obligati sunt et ceciderunt,* etc. *Ipsi* rerum temporalium cupiditate *obligati sunt:* timentes parcere Domino, ne a Romanis perderent locum, et irruentes in lapidem offensionis et petram scandali, de spe coelesti ceciderunt, quibus caecitas ex parte Israel facta est, ignorantibus Dei justitiam, et suam volentibus constituere: nos vero, ut plenitudo gentium intraret, de lapidibus excitati filii Abraham, qui non sectabamur justitiam, apprehendimus [0793B] eam, et *surreximus,* nec viribus nostris, sed per fidem justificati *erecti sumus.*

VERS. 10.-- *Domine, salvum fac regem,* etc. *Domine, salvum fac regem,* et ipse, qui nobis exemplum praeliandi passione sua monstravit, offerat etiam sacrificia nostra sacerdos excitatus a mortuis, quo jam pro nobis offerente, *exaudi nos in die qua invocaverimus te.*

## IN PSALMUM XX.

Titulus notus est: de Christo canitur.

VERS. 2.-- *Domine, in virtute tua laetabitur rex,* etc. *Domine, in virtute tua,* quod Verbum caro factum, laetabitur homo Christus Jesus, *et super hoc,* quod vivificas omnia, *exsultavit vehementer.*

VERS. 3.-- *Desiderium cordis ejus tribuisti ei,* etc. [0793C] Desideravit manducare Pascha, et ponere cum vellet, atque iterum sumere animam suam, et dedisti ei; *pacem meam,* inquit, *relinquo vobis,* et factum est.

VERS. 4.-- *Quoniam praevenisti eum in benedictionibus dulcedinis,* etc. Quoniam prius hauserat *benedictionem dulcedinis* tuae, fel peccatorum nostrorum non nocuit ei, quem in principio sermonis ejus accedentes ambierunt lapides pretiosi, discipuli sui, a quibus exordium annuntiationis ejus fieret.

VERS. 5.-- *Vitam petiit a te, et tribuisti ei longitudinem dierum,* etc. Resurrectionem petiit dicens: *Pater, clarifica Filium tuum:* et dedisti ei longa tempora saeculi hujus, quae haberet Ecclesia, et deinceps aeternitatem *in saeculum saeculi.*

VERS. 6.-- *Magna est gloria ejus in salutari tuo,* [0793D] etc. *Magna est* quidem *gloria ejus* in salute, qua eum resuscitasti; sed adhuc *gloria et magnum decorem* [0794A] addes ei, cum in coelo collocabis ad dexteram tuam.

VERS. 7.-- *Quoniam dabis eum in benedictionem,* etc. Haec est *benedictio* quam *dabis* ei *in saeculum saeculi: laetificabis eum in gaudio cum vultu tuo* secundum hominem, quem levavit ad te.

VERS. 8.-- *Quoniam rex sperat in Domino,* etc. *Quoniam rex* non superbit, sed humilis corde *sperat in Domino, et in misericordia Altissimi non conturbabitur,* humilians se, et obediens usque ad mortem crucis.

VERS. 9.-- *Inveniatur manus tua omnibus inimicis tuis,* etc. *Inveniatur,* o rex, potestas tua, cum ad judicandum veneris, *omnibus inimicis tuis,* qui eam in humilitate tua non intellexerunt, claritasque, qua [0794B] regnas ad dexteram Patris, *inveniat* in die judicii puniendos, *qui te oderunt,* quia nunc ipsi non invenerunt eam.

VERS. 10.-- *Pones eos ut clibanum ignis,* etc. Constitues eos ardentes intrinsecus conscientia impietatis suae in tempore manifestationis tuae: deinde conturbati vindicta Domini post accusationem conscientiae dabuntur aeterno devorandi incendio.

VERS. 11.-- *Fructum eorum de terra perdes,* etc. *Fructum eorum,* quia terrenus est, *perdes de terra,* et opera illorum, et quoscunque seduxerunt, non deputabis inter filios hominum, quos in haereditatem sempiternam vocasti.

VERS. 12.-- *Quoniam declinaverunt in te mala,* etc. [0794C] Haec poena retribuetur eis, quoniam mala, quae sibi imminere te regnante arbitrabantur, in te occidendum retorserunt, cogitaveruntque consilia dicentes: *Expedit unum pro omnibus mori.* Et: *Venite, occidamus eum, et habemus haereditatem ejus.* Quae idcirco *non potuerunt stabilire,* nescientes quid dixerint, nec adepti, quod cupierunt.

VERS. 13.-- *Quoniam pones eos dorsum,* etc. Quoniam ordinabis eos in his, a quibus postpositis et contemptis averteris, et in his, quae relinquis, id est cupiditatibus regni terreni, praeparabis tibi ad passionem impudentiam eorum.

VERS. 14.-- *Exaltare, Domine, in virtute tua,* etc. O *Domine,* quem humilem non cognoverunt, *exaltare in virtute tua,* quam infirmitatem putaverunt. [0794D] Nos autem corde et opere celebrabimus, et nota faciemus mirabilia tua.

## PEZ'S PRELIMINARY NOTICE.

[0751C]

« Among our men of Reichenau there occurs an Exposition on seventy-six psalms by Walafrid the abbot, beginning from the first in this manner: *All Scripture divinely inspired, of the Old and of the New Testament, unto the imitation of the Mediator of God and men, the man Jesus Christ,* etc., the other volume seems to have been lost. » Thus far John Mabillon, volume IV of the Analecta, page 633. Following his authority, I left no effort unspent among our most distinguished men of Reichenau, that they might kindly communicate to me this Exposition of their own Walafrid, a man by far the most celebrated in the ninth century for learning and for virtue, drawn out of the darkness. In which matter I found those learned and diligent men the more indulgent and the readier, the surer the hope they conceived that by that labour of theirs something not inconsiderable would be of service to the Catholic Church. And so they sent to me the entire Exposition of all seventy-six psalms, skilfully and correctly transcribed, the whole business being seen to by the distinguished and most erudite Dom P. Apronian Hueber, prior of Mehrerau, and I had promised [0751D] my friends a speedy edition of it in my Thesaurus. Nor would I ever have changed my mind, had I not, upon a thorough examination of the work, discovered that the kernel and the marrow of Walafrid's commentary had long since been set before the learned in the Glossa ordinaria, which likewise has Walafrid Strabo for its author. Therefore, lest I should be too burdensome to those learned men who, on other grounds, desire me to be not inconsiderably more sparing [sic: *partiorem*] in the serving up of theological matters, I determined to insert into my Thesaurus nothing but the exposition of the first twenty psalms, as it were by way of a specimen of the remaining work. But if any erudite men shall observe, from this specimen, a greater difference between Walafrid's exposition of the psalms and the ordinary Gloss upon the same than I have observed, and shall judge that it will be worth the labour if by the same method the explanation of the remaining [0752C] psalms also be published: I shall comply with them in the volumes that follow the more readily, inasmuch as it is the more equitable that so great a labour of the friends of Reichenau, destined for the common advantage and use, should not utterly perish.



## ON PSALM THE FIRST.

VERS. 1, 2.-- *Blessed is the man who hath not gone away in the counsel of the ungodly, and hath not stood in the way of sinners: and hath not sat in the chair of pestilence. But in the law of the Lord,* etc.

All Scripture of the Old and of the New Testament, divinely inspired, invites the faithful to the imitation of the Mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus, that through imitation we may deserve to come to his likeness. As he himself saith: *If any man minister to me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also shall my minister [0752D] be.* So the apostle and evangelist John: *Dearly beloved,* he saith, *now we are the sons of God, and it hath not yet appeared what we shall be: we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like to him, because we shall see him as he is.* Thus therefore this first psalm also teaches believers to follow the author and the bestower of true blessedness, by turning aside from evil and doing good, that they may come to his likeness and may become *as a tree planted beside the running waters.*

But he turns aside from evil perfectly who neither delights in his heart, nor acts in deed, nor teaches others, that they should [0753A] do so. For this is *not to go away in the counsel of the ungodly, nor to stand in the way of sinners, nor to sit in the chair of pestilence;* but rather *to meditate in the law of the Lord,* not of necessity but of will, without ceasing, which is what *day and night* signifies. Or, as Scripture is wont, it sets *day* for prosperity and *night* for adversity: so that neither the gladness of temporal things nor the adversity of transitory things may turn the mind of him who follows the Lord away from the meditation of the divine law. And how necessary that is, is shown there also, where the Lord commanded Josue, the minister and confidant of the lawgiver, who had learned the law first and foremost, that he should not forsake the *volume of the law,* but should meditate in it *day and night, that he may direct his way and may understand all the things which it saith.*

[0753B]But if any man asks more openly what the *counsel of the ungodly* is, [cj: *quod si*; read *quod sit*, "what the counsel is"] Scripture speaks of it in manifold ways, and most of all the book which is called of Wisdom, where it saith: *The ungodly said within themselves, not thinking aright.* [var: Vulg. Sap 2:1 *Dixerunt enim cogitantes apud se non recte*, without the word for "the ungodly"] And a little after: *Come, and let us enjoy the good things that are, and let us use the creature as in youth, speedily.* And again: *Let us oppress the poor just man, nor let us reverence the grey hairs of the aged, of long time,* etc.

But the *way of sinners* is that of which the Psalmist elsewhere, after such things, subjoins: *This their way is a stumbling-block to them.* And the Lord saith: *Broad is the way which leadeth to death. But the chair of pestilence* [var: Vulg. Mt 7:13 has *perditionem*, "perdition", where Migne has "death"] signifies perverse doctrine, which comes about in two ways: either by inviting openly to the wickedness of works, as Solomon shows in the Proverbs, saying: *My son, if [0753C] sinners shall entice thee, consent not to them: if they shall say: Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us hide snares against the innocent without cause,* etc. Or by leading into error, as follows there after some things, where he also names this chair a *seat,* saying: *A foolish woman, and clamorous, and full of allurements, and knowing nothing at all, sat at the doors of her house upon a seat.* And a little after: *Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread more pleasant:* which without doubt signify perverse doctrine: for the reprobate follow after all these things so far, and by following them so spurn and execrate the meditation of the divine law, that, according to the Prophet, they hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and abhor him that speaketh perfectly, and say to God: *Depart from us, and we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.*

[0753D]This order, which this first psalm shows, comprehending most fully in brief what evils are to be turned aside from and what goods are to be done, Holy Scripture keeps in many places: as that saying of the blessed apostle James is like to this: *Casting away all uncleanness and abundance of malice, with meekness receive the ingrafted word, which is able to save your souls.* And again: *Resist the devil, and he will fly from you: draw nigh to the Lord, and he will draw nigh to you.* Which order also the Church most solemnly keeps in the sacraments of those who are born again of water and the Holy Spirit, that first they renounce the devil and all his pomps or works, and afterwards profess that they believe in God the Father almighty, and in Jesus [0754A] Christ his Son, and in the Holy Spirit, and the Catholic Church, and the remission of sins; and so are dipped in the saving water and are incorporated into the Church (outside of which, even if a man should have done the things said above, he shall not be able to be saved), and, made members of the tree of life, begin to tend toward its likeness. Which the blessed Paul shows, in agreement with the words that follow, saying: *As many of us as are baptized in Christ Jesus, are baptized in his death: for we are buried together with him by baptism into death, that as Christ rose again from the dead by the glory of the Father: so we also may walk in newness. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also of his resurrection.*

VERS. 3.-- *And he shall be as,* etc. Of this tree [0754B] he spoke concerning himself in the time of his passion: *If in the green wood they do these things, what shall be done in the dry?* If the transgressor shall stretch out his hand to this tree and take of its fruit, he shall live for ever. Which also in the Apocalypse he promises to him that overcometh, saying: *To him that overcometh I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God.*

*But by the running of the waters,* understand either the Holy Spirit, as the Evangelist writes that the Lord said: *He that believeth in me, as the Scripture saith, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.* Which, expounding it, he subjoins, saying: *Now this he said of the Spirit which they should receive who believed in him.* By whose working was wrought the very incarnation of the Saviour, according to that which the angel Gabriel speaks to Joseph [0754C] concerning the blessed Mother of God, Mary, saying: *Fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is born in her is of the Holy Spirit.* Or the utterances of the Scriptures, which foretold the coming of the just one, and the sufferings to be in Christ, and the glories that should follow after, as the same just and justifying Lord speaks to the apostles after his resurrection, saying: *These are the words which I spoke to you when I was yet with you: for it is necessary that all things be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.* And: *Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures,* that out of them they might take the vital moisture which they should minister to believers, according to that which the Prophet promises them, saying: *You shall draw waters with joy out of the fountains of the Saviour.* For that the *divine utterances* [0754D] are signified by the name of waters, the same Scripture testifies in many places: of which one is: *Words out of the mouth of a man are deep water, and the fountain of wisdom an overflowing torrent.*

But the *fruit* and the *leaves of this tree* are the things which Jesus began to do and to teach: of whom certain of the disciples were speaking: *Who was a man, a prophet, mighty in work and in word before God and all the people.*

But that which he says *in his time,* the Apostle expounded, saying: *When the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, that he might redeem them who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons:* which are the fruits of the tree.

And that which he subjoins: *and his leaf shall not fall off,* signifies the unmoved firmness of his words. So [0755A] he himself saith: *Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.*

But concerning the *prosperity of his doings* the Father also promises through Isaias: *My word, which shall go forth out of my mouth, shall not return to me void: but it shall do whatsoever I willed, and shall prosper in those things for which I sent it.*

VERS. 4.-- *Not so the ungodly,* etc. *The ungodly are not so,* in the manner of those who by imitation so far advance unto the likeness of the tree of life that, by seeing its blessedness and its eternity, they are themselves blessed and eternal, according to that which God promises through Isaias the prophet, saying: *For according to the days of the tree shall be the days of my people.*

*But as dust* dry and unfruitful, inasmuch as [0755B] they are strangers to the moisture of the waters spoken of above, they are cast forth from the solidity and the stability of the earth of the present, that is, of the Church, and of that which is to come, into the wind, and being cast forth they stand as food for the serpent, of which it is written: *And dust is the serpent's bread. But the wind* itself is understood to be the devil, as it is written: *The north is a hard wind.* And by the name *right hand* is he called, who in the prophet is also called the spirit of fornication: and by the Apostle he is named *the spirit that now worketh in the children of unbelief.*

VERS. 5.-- *Therefore the ungodly shall not rise,* etc. If any difference is here to be taken between the *ungodly and sinners,* by the *ungodly* are to be understood those of whom the Lord says: *He that believeth not in the Son is already judged. But sinners,* to whom the Judge is to say: *Depart from [0755C] me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire.* Who indeed *shall rise in judgment,* but not *in the council of the just,* as the Lord threatens certain men through Ezechiel the prophet, saying: *They shall not be in the council of my people, that in the writing of the house of Israel they shall not be written, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel.* [var: Vulg. Ezech 13:9 *et in scriptura domus Israel non scribentur*, "and they shall not be written"; Migne's *ut* does not construe with the future indicative]

VERS. 6.-- *For the Lord hath known,* etc. *He hath known,* that is, he approves, and praising it rewards the doings of the just: as through Solomon he promises that he will say to the Church in the universal judgment: *Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.* In the gates, namely, in the entrance of the heavenly kingdom: which gates or doors are shut to the foolish virgins, who shall remain among those whose *way shall perish.* For both what perishes the Lord [0755D] says that he knows not, and what the Lord knows not, perishes: as also to the foolish virgins aforesaid, and to those who shall say: *Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name?* etc., the Judge himself says that he will answer. *Amen I say to you, I know you not;* or: *I never knew you.*



## ON PSALM II.

VERS. 1.-- *Why have the gentiles raged, and the peoples meditated vain things,* etc. It is a question of rebuking. For the prophet chides the peoples. *Why have they raged* against the Lord the Saviour, when they had no causes of anger? But he says that they meditated *vain things,* because they did not accomplish what they wished, namely that Christ should be extinguished.

[0756A]VERS. 2.-- *The kings stood up,* etc. This is said of the persecutors of the Lord, who are also commemorated in the Acts of the Apostles. But *they stood up* signifies not presence, but will.

VERS. 3.-- *Let us break asunder their bonds,* etc. Although it can be taken otherwise also, yet it is more fitly taken from the person of those whom he said had meditated vain things, so that this is *let us break asunder their bonds,* let us take pains that they bind us not, nor that the Christian religion be laid upon us. But *theirs,* either of God the Father and of his Christ, or of Christ and of the apostles.

VERS. 4.-- *He that dwelleth in the heavens,* etc. The sentence is repeated. For in place of that which is, *He that dwelleth in the heavens,* there is set afterwards: *the Lord.* In place of that which is, *shall laugh at them,* there is set afterwards, *shall deride them.* [0756B] None of these things ought to be understood carnally, as though God laughed with cheeks or derided with the nose; but that force is to be taken which he gives to his saints, that, discerning things to come, that is, the name of Christ and his dominion about to spread abroad among those who come after and to lay hold of all nations, they may understand that those men meditated vain things. For this force, by which those things were foreknown, is the laughter of God and the derision. But by the *heavens* we take holy souls, through whom, since they indeed foreknow what shall come to pass, God will deride and mock.

VERS. 5.-- *Then shall he speak,* etc. The *anger and fury* of God must be understood not as a perturbation of his; but as the force by which he most justly takes vengeance, all creation being subject to him for his ministry. Although the *anger of God* may rightly be understood also as that very darkening of the mind which [0756C] follows upon those who transgress the law of God.

VERS. 6.-- *But I am appointed,* etc. Some interpret Sion as *watching,* which we ought to take as the Church, where daily the intention of watching upon the charity of God is raised up. Which is also called a *mountain* because of its eminence and its firmness.

VERS. 7.-- *The Lord said to me,* etc. That day may seem to be spoken of in the prophecy on which Jesus Christ was born according to the man. Yet because *to-day* signifies a present, and in eternity there is neither anything past, as though it had ceased to be, nor future, as though it were not yet, *to-day* may also be understood, by a most sincere and Catholic faith, of the everlasting generation of the power and the wisdom of God, who is the only-begotten Son.

[0756D]VERS. 8.-- *Ask of me,* etc. Namely, that the nations may be joined to the Christian name, and so be redeemed from death, that they may be possessed by God.

VERS. 9.-- *Thou shalt rule them with a rod,* etc. *With a rod of iron,* in inflexible justice, crushing in them earthly desires and the miry businesses of the old man.

VERS. 10.-- *And now, ye kings,* etc. *And now,* that is, now made new: for they are signified as spiritual who *judge the earth:* for whatever we judge is beneath us: but whatever is beneath the spiritual man is deservedly named *earth.*

VERS. 11.-- *Serve ye the Lord,* etc. Most excellently is *rejoice* subjoined, lest that which was said, *serve,* should seem to avail unto misery. But again, lest that same thing should incline [0757A] into an outpouring of rashness, there is added, *with trembling,* that it might avail unto a circumspect wariness.

VERS.12.-- *Embrace ye discipline,* etc. To understand and to be instructed, this is *to embrace discipline.* But in that which is said, *embrace ye,* there is signified sufficiently that there is a certain defence and fortification against all the things which could hurt, unless it were embraced with so great care. But *to perish* from *the just way* is a great punishment, which is dreaded by those who have perceived something of the sweetness of justice.

VERS.13.-- *When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time,* etc. That is, when the vengeance shall come which is prepared for the ungodly and for sinners, it shall not only not touch those who *trust in the Lord,* but shall even profit them unto that blessedness where is the sum and the heaping up of all good things. But that [0757B] which is set down: *in a short time,* I judge to signify this, that it will be something sudden, when sinners reckon it remote and far off in time to come.

## ON PSALM III.

VERS. 1.-- *A psalm of David, when he fled from the face of his son Absalom.*

*David,* who is interpreted *strong of hand* or *desirable,* signifies our Lord Jesus Christ, whose voice is brought in in this psalm speaking of his passion and his resurrection. But *Absalom* signifies Judas the betrayer, or the persecuting people. For Judas also was still among the apostles when the Lord said: *The children of the bridegroom cannot fast, so long as the bridegroom is with them.* [var: Vulg. Mt 9:15 *lugere*, "to mourn"; "fast" is Mark's word at Mc 2:19] And of the people he says through Moses [0757C]: *A firstborn son among Israel.* [var: Vulg. Ex 4:22 *Filius meus primogenitus Israel*, "Israel is my firstborn son"] The Truth therefore fled the mind of Judas, or of the persecuting people, while it did not cease to enlighten them. Or, as the Gospel narrates: *These things Jesus spoke, and he went away and hid himself from them.* But whereas Absalom is interpreted *the Father's peace,* it is well understood that Christ showed peace to his betrayer, although that man was laid waste by the inward war of so wicked a thought: and toward the persecuting people he stood so appeased that he besought the Father for them, saying: *Father, pardon them, for they know not what they do.* [var: Vulg. Lc 23:34 *dimitte*, "forgive"]

VERS. 2.-- *Lord, why are they multiplied,* etc. So greatly, namely, *are they multiplied,* that even out of the number of the disciples there was not wanting one who joined the number of the persecutors.

VERS. 3.-- *Many say,* etc. It is manifest [0757D] that unless they had despaired of his rising again, they would certainly not have killed him. Therefore neither would Judas have betrayed him, unless he had been of the number of those who despised Christ, saying: *There is no salvation for him in his God.*

VERS. 4.-- *But thou, O Lord, art my protector,* etc. He too calls the Lord his *glory,* whom the Word of God so took up that together with him he became God. But *head* I think is here to be taken as the human mind itself, which so cleaved to, and in a manner grew together with, the excellent supereminence of the Word taking up the man, that in so great a lowliness of the passion it was not laid down.

These things can also be taken from the person of the Church. For in that man the Church also was taken up by the Word, which was made flesh and dwelt among us. Let therefore [0758A] the Church speak together with her head, set amid the storms of persecutions throughout the whole round of the earth: *Lord, why are they multiplied,* etc., her head being exalted, who as the firstborn from the dead ascended into heaven.

VERS. 5.-- *With my voice I have cried to the Lord,* etc. Not with the voice of the body, which is put forth with the noise of beaten air, but with the voice of the heart, which is silent to men, but sounds to God as a cry, when the soul alone, drawing nothing of the flesh and nothing of fleshly intentions into the prayer, speaks to the Lord where he alone hears. And this too is called a cry because of the force of the intention itself.

But he says that the Father heard him *from the mountain,* that is, from his own justice. For it was just that he should raise up [0758B] from the dead one slain though innocent, and to whom evils were repaid for good things, and should repay worthy things to his persecutors: For we read: *Thy justice is as the mountains of God.* But the Church also is heard from that same mountain, which is likewise her head, of which the Prophet says: *The mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains.*

VERS. 6.-- *I have slept,* etc. Not unfittingly may *I* be noted, to signify that of his own will he underwent death, according to that: *Therefore doth the Father love me, because I lay down my life, and I shall take it again: no man shall take it away from myself.* And it is well taken: *I have slept and have taken my rest:* I gave myself over to the passion, and death followed. To the people of the Church also it is said: *Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall touch thee,* [var: Vulg. Eph 5:14 *illuminabit te Christus*, "Christ shall enlighten thee"] because he was taken up from among sinners. *I will not fear [0758C] thousands,* etc. It is not to a God sleeping, not to a God lying down, that it is said, *arise:* but it is the manner of the divine Scriptures to attribute to the person of God what he works in us, not indeed everywhere, but where it can fittingly be said: or that he himself be said to speak, when by his gift the several messengers of truth speak.

VERS. 7.-- *For thou hast struck all them,* etc. They are broken, that is, brought to nothing, the words of sinners tearing and cursing the Son of God. The *teeth of sinners* can also be taken as the princes of sinners, by whose authority a man is now cut off from the fellowship of those living rightly, and as it were incorporated with those living ill.

VERS. 8.-- *O Lord, there is salvation,* etc. [var: Vulg. Ps 3:9 *Domini est salus*, "salvation is the Lord's"] Let no man therefore presume of himself, since it is the Lord's to save from [0758D] the death of sin. But do thou, O Lord, bless thy people, that hopeth in thee for salvation.



## ON PSALM IV.

VERS. 2.-- *When I called upon him he heard me,* etc. *O God of my justice,* from whom is my justice, thou hast led me from the straits of sadness into the breadth of joys: *For tribulation and anguish upon every soul of man that worketh evil.* But he who says: *We rejoice in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience, and patience trial, and trial hope; and hope confoundeth not, because the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who is given to us,* [var: Vulg. Rom 5:3 *gloriamur*, "we glory"] has no straits of the heart, [0759A] although from without they are heaped upon him by persecutors. But this voice is either of the Lord Jesus Christ after his resurrection: or of the Church believing and hoping in him: *Have mercy on me and hear,* etc. The devoted mother says that mercy is to be had upon herself, if for her sons the prayer be heard, since whatever is granted to the members is without doubt bestowed upon the whole body.

VERS. 3.-- *Ye sons of men,* etc. At the least *until* the coming of the Son of God will your error have lasted: why then are you further *heavy of heart?* When will you have an end of deceits, if you have not the presence of the truth? For since the truth alone, out of which all things are true, makes men blessed, why are you detained by the love of temporal things, why do you follow after the last things as though they were the first, which is vanity and a lie? For you desire that to abide [0759B] with you which all passes away as a shadow.

VERS. 4.-- *And know ye that,* etc. Whom, save him whom he raised up from the dead below and set in heaven at his right hand? The human race therefore is rebuked, that they may at length turn themselves to him from the love of this world; and that, as they rejoice over the illumination in this life, so they may know that they must pray for rest after this life.

VERS. 5.-- *Be ye angry and do not,* etc. It can be understood in two ways. Either: Even if *ye are angry, sin not,* that is, even if there arises a motion of the soul which now, because of the punishment of sin, is not in one's power, at least let not reason and the mind consent to it, which within has been regenerated [0759C] according to God, so that with the mind we may serve the law of God, if with the flesh we still serve the law of sin. Or: Do penance, that is, *be angry* with your own selves for past sins, and cease to sin further.

And that which follows: *which you say in your hearts,* is a full sentence: what you say in your hearts, say ye, that is, be not the people of which it was said: *With the lips they honour me, but their heart is far from me. Chambers*, moreover, are the hearts themselves, of which the Lord also warns us that we pray within, the doors being shut. [var: Vulg. Ps 4:5 *in cubilibus vestris*, "in your couches"]

VERS. 6.-- *Sacrifice ye the sacrifice,* etc. He says the same in another psalm: *A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit.* Wherefore it is not absurdly taken here that this is the *sacrifice of justice* which is made through penance. For what is more just than that each man should be angry rather at his own sins [0759D] than at another's, and, punishing himself, should slay himself to God? Or else the *sacrifice of justice* is just works after penance.

But *many* are foolish, who doubt or despair of that very life to come which is promised to us, who often say: *Who knoweth whether these things be true, or who hath come back from the dead below to bring word of them?*

VERS. 7.-- *It is signed upon us,* etc. This light is the whole and true good of man, which is beheld not with the eyes but with the mind. But he said it was *signed* in us, as a penny is signed with the image of the king. For man was made to the likeness and image of God, which by sinning he corrupted. His good therefore is true and eternal, if by being born again he be signed. Therefore it is not [0760A] without that *gladness* is to be sought, but within, where the light of the countenance of God is signed.

VERS. 8.-- *By the fruit of their corn,* etc. It is not idle that *their own* is added; for there is a *corn and wine and oil* of God also. But these men, given over to temporal pleasures, ever burn with desires and cannot be satisfied: and, stretched out with manifold and toilsome thinking, they are not suffered to see the simple good. The faithful man therefore rejoices and says:

VERS. 9.-- *In peace in the selfsame,* etc. For rightly is there hoped for by such men an utter estrangement of the mind from mortal things, and a forgetting of the miseries of this world, which is fittingly and prophetically signified by the name of falling asleep and of sleep, where the highest peace can be broken in upon by no tumult. But this [0760B] is to be hoped for after this life. Wherefore he fitly adds the last thing, and says:

VERS. 10.-- *For thou, O Lord, singularly,* etc. Well does he say, *singularly:* for it can be referred against those many who, multiplied by the fruit of their corn, of their wine and of their oil, say: *Who sheweth us good things?* For this manifoldness perishes, and *singularly* is it held in the saints, of whom it is said: *And of the multitude of believers there was one soul and heart.* [var: Vulg. Act 4:32 *cor unum et anima una*, "one heart and one soul"]



## ON PSALM V.

VERS. 1.-- *Unto the end, for her that obtaineth the truth, a psalm of David.* [var: Vulg. Ps 5:1 *pro ea quae haereditatem consequitur*, "for her that obtaineth the inheritance"] The Church is understood, which receives the inheritance unto life everlasting through our Lord Jesus Christ, that she may possess God himself, [0760C] cleaving to whom she may be blessed, according to that: *The Lord is the portion of my inheritance.* Wherefore it is the voice of the Church called unto the inheritance, and that she herself may become the inheritance of God.

VERS. 2.-- *Give ear to my words,* etc. Well does he show what that *cry* is: since indeed the voice of the body is heard, but the spiritual voice is understood.

VERS. 3.-- *Hearken to the voice,* etc. The Scriptures are wont to call the Son a king. According to that therefore which was said: *Through me is the going to the Father,* assuredly first *my king,* and then *my God.*

VERS. 4, 5.-- *For to thee will I pray, O Lord,* etc. *In the morning I will stand before thee,* etc. Thou art not, he says, such a one as could be seen by those from whose eyes the night of sins has not yet departed. My night of error being ended, and the [0760D] darkness departing which by my sins I made for myself, *thou wilt hear my voice.*

But *I will stand,* what is it but: I will not lie down? And to lie down is to rest upon the earth, which is to seek blessedness from earthly pleasures. We must not therefore cleave to earthly things, if we wish to see God, who is beheld by the pure.

VERS. 6.-- *Neither shall he dwell,* etc. That is, they shall not so see him as to cleave to him, because their mind is beaten back by the light of truth on account of the darkness of sins, by the habit of which they cannot bear the brightness of right understanding.

VERS. 7.-- *Thou hatest all them that work,* etc. He hates those whom he does not suffer to abide in himself: and they do not abide [0761A] who have not strength to bear him. But *a lie* is contrary to truth. Yet lest any man think that some substance or nature is contrary to truth, let him understand that a lie pertains to that which is not, not to that which is. For if that is said which is, the truth is said: but if that is said which is not, it is a lie. Therefore he begins: *Thou wilt destroy them that speak a lie,* because, departing from that which is, they turn aside to that which is not.

*The bloody and deceitful man,* etc. Understand *the bloody man* as him that worketh iniquity, [cj: *operantur*; read *operantem*, "him that worketh"] and *the deceitful* as him that loveth a lie. But the *abominated* are wont to be called the disinherited. And this psalm is *for her that obtaineth the inheritance,* who subjoins the exultation of her hope, saying:

[0761B]VERS. 8.-- *I will go into the house,* etc. *I will go into thy house:* it is said, I believe, as a stone into a building. For what else is the house of God than the temple of God, of which it is said: *For the temple of God is holy, which you are.* Of which building the corner-stone is he whom the power co-eternal with the Father, and the wisdom of God, took up.

But it must be considered that he did not say: *in the temple,* but: *to the temple:* for the holy temple is the body of the Lord and Saviour, which the Church rightly adores: of which he himself said: *Destroy this temple.* And he adds: *in thy fear,* which is a great safeguard to those going forward unto salvation.

VERS. 9.-- *O Lord, lead me,* etc. Nothing is more manifest than that he commends that time in which he advances: [0761C] for this is the journey which is accomplished not by places of the earth, but by the affections of the mind. *In thy sight,* he says, *my way,* according to that which is said also in the Lord's prayer: *Hallowed be thy name;* not that it should be hallowed for us who pray, which is holy of itself; but that we may ask that what is holy by its own nature be hallowed in us also. Therefore now also the Prophet asks that the way of God, which is right of itself, may be made right for himself too.

VERS. 10.-- *For there is no truth in their mouth,* etc. How can truth be in the mouth of those whose heart is deceived concerning sin and the punishment of sin?

VERS. 11.-- *A sepulchre,* etc. Flatterers and heretics are called *open sepulchres,* because, since they themselves are dead by not having the life of truth, into themselves [0761D] they receive the dead, whom they slay with lying words. But in that he says: *Judge them, O God,* he does not wish that it may come to pass, but discerns what is to come.

*Let them fall away,* etc. *Let them fall away,* their own thoughts accusing them, their own conscience: and because they are greatly ungodly, drive them far away from that inheritance which is possessed by understanding and seeing God.

VERS. 12.-- *And let them be glad,* etc. He himself therefore will be the everlasting exultation, as the just become the temple of God.

*And they shall glory,* etc. This is the blessing: to glory in God and to be inhabited by God.

VERS. 13.-- *O Lord, as with a shield of thy good will,* etc. The good will of God goes before our will, that he may call sinners to repentance. And these are the arms [0762A] by which the enemy is stormed, against whom it is said: *Who shall accuse against the elect of God?* And again: *For if, when as yet we were enemies, Christ died for us, much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved from wrath through him.* This most unconquerable shield, by which the enemy is driven away, suggesting despair of salvation by the multitude of tribulations and of temptations.



## ON PSALM VI.

VERS. 1.-- *Unto the end, in songs, for the octave, a psalm of David.* The day of judgment can be understood as the eighth, in that eternal life is now received after the end of this world. Then the souls of the just will not be subject to times. And since all times are rolled round by the repetition of the seven days of the just, that day is perhaps said [0762B] to be the eighth which will not have this variety, which, rendering to merits what is owed, carries the saints over into eternal life, but condemns the ungodly everlastingly. Fearing which condemnation, the Church prays, saying:

VERS. 2.-- *Lord, not in thy fury,* etc. In the day of judgment *they are rebuked,* that is, accused, all who have not the foundation, which is Christ. But *they are chastised,* that is, purged, who build upon this foundation wood, hay, stubble, and yet shall be saved, so as by fire. But this man prays that in the Lord's anger he may neither be condemned nor amended, but be so perfectly healed here that he may not only not fear death, but may not even have to bear the hand of the physician that burns or cuts. And so he goes on and says:

VERS. 3.-- *Have mercy on me, O God,* etc. [var: Vulg. Ps 6:3 *Miserere mei, Domine*, "Have mercy on me, O Lord"] That is the firmness [0762C] of the soul, or its strength: for this is what *bones* signify. Wherefore what is subjoined belongs to the exposition:

VERS. 4.-- *And my soul,* etc. Who would not understand a soul struggling with her own diseases, but long put off by the physician, so that she might be convinced into what evils she had flung herself by sinning? For what is easily healed is not much guarded against. But out of the difficulty of the healing there will be a more diligent keeping of the health recovered.

VERS. 5.-- *Turn, O Lord,* etc. Turning himself, he prays that God also may turn to him, as it is said: *Turn ye to me, and I will turn to you, saith the Lord.*

VERS. 6.-- *For there is not,* etc. He understands that now is the time of conversion, because, when this life has passed, [0762D] nothing remains but the recompense of merits. That too can be understood in this way, that by *death* he means the sin which is committed when the law of God is despised. In which death, that is, to be unmindful of God, to despise the law and the commandments, so that by *hell* he has meant the blindness of mind which receives the sinner, that is, the dying man, and wraps him about. From that death and from that hell the soul beseeches that she be kept safe, while she labours at conversion to the Lord and feels the difficulties. Wherefore she weaves on, saying:

VERS. 7.-- *I have laboured,* etc. *A bed* is in this place the name given to that in which a sick and feeble mind takes its rest, that is, in the pleasure of the body and in every worldly delight, and he *washes it with tears* who strives to drag himself [0763A] out of it, and is forced to suffer, as it were, days and nights by an alternating affection: so that, when he says: *with the mind I serve the law of God,* he feels as it were day: again when he says: *but with the flesh the law of sin,* he is bent down into night, until all night pass and one day come, of which it is said: *in the morning I will stand before thee.* And this *couch* we take to be the same as the bed: although *I will water* is something more than *I will wash:* since a thing can be washed on the surface, whereas watering reaches to the inward parts, which signifies weeping that goes to the innermost places of the heart.

VERS. 8.-- *It is troubled,* etc. Because of the Lord's anger he professes that the *eye* of his heart is *troubled.* For what is more to be dreaded than that he should be angry who, if he does not have mercy, destroys?
